Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “cook‑book” that you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or adapt to your own workflow). It covers every step you listed: | Step | What to do | Commands / File contents | |------|------------|--------------------------| | **1. Clone the repo** | | `git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git` | | **2. Analyse & create artefacts** | | | | 2.1 | **Dockerfile** | Create `Dockerfile` in the repo root with the following content: | | | | ```dockerfile
# Use official Node.js LTS image as base
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files and install dependencies (cached layer)
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on (default 3000)
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
``` | | 2.2 | **Kubernetes YAML** | Create `k8s/deployment.yaml` (you can keep it in a `k8s/` folder or at the repo root). Use the helper function if you want, but here’s the raw YAML: | | | | ```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
replicas: 2
selector:
matchLabels:
app: nodejs-welcome
template:
metadata:
labels:
app: nodejs-welcome
spec:
containers:
- name: nodejs-welcome
image: /nodejs-welcome:latest
ports:
- containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
selector:
app: nodejs-welcome
ports:
- protocol: TCP
port: 80
targetPort: 3000
type: ClusterIP
``` | | 2.3 | **GitHub Actions** | Create `.github/workflows/docker-build.yml` with the following content: | | | | ```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker image
on:
push:
branches: [ main ]
jobs:
build:
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
steps:
- name: Checkout repository
uses: actions/checkout@v4
- name: Set up Docker Buildx
uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
- name: Log in to Docker Hub
uses: docker/login-action@v3
with:
username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
- name: Build and push image
uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
with:
context: .
push: true
tags: /nodejs-welcome:latest
``` | | **3. Add all changed files** | | `git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml` | | **4. Commit & push** | | `git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"`
`git push origin main` | --- ### Quick notes 1. **Docker image name** – Replace `` with your actual Docker Hub username. If you don’t have a Docker Hub account yet, create one at https://hub.docker.com/ and generate a *Personal Access Token* (PAT). Store the username and token as GitHub secrets named `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` and `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` in the repository settings. 2. **Kubernetes namespace** – The YAML above deploys into the default namespace. If you want a dedicated namespace, add `namespace: ` under `metadata:` in both the Deployment and Service sections. 3. **Port mapping** – The Node.js app listens on port `3000` inside the container. The Service exposes it on port `80` externally. Adjust if your app uses a different port. 4. **CI workflow** – The workflow triggers on every push to `main`. It builds the Docker image and pushes it to Docker Hub. If you prefer to tag images with the Git SHA or a timestamp, modify the `tags:` line accordingly. 5. **Testing locally** – After pushing, you can test the Docker image locally: ```bash docker pull /nodejs-welcome:latest docker run -p 3000:3000 /nodejs-welcome:latest ``` 6. **Deploying to a cluster** – Once the image is on Docker Hub, apply the manifests: ```bash kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml ``` --- ### Full script you can paste into a terminal ```bash # 1. Clone the repo git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git cd nodejs-welcome # 2.1 Create Dockerfile cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF' # Use official Node.js LTS image as base FROM node:18-alpine AS builder # Set working directory WORKDIR /app # Copy package files and install dependencies (cached layer) COPY package*.json ./ RUN npm ci --only=production # Copy source code COPY . . # Expose the port the app listens on (default 3000) EXPOSE 3000 # Start the application CMD ["node", "app.js"] EOF # 2.2 Create Kubernetes manifests mkdir -p k8s cat > k8s/deployment.yaml <<'EOF' apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: nodejs-welcome-deployment spec: replicas: 2 selector: matchLabels: app: nodejs-welcome template: metadata: labels: app: nodejs-welcome spec: containers: - name: nodejs-welcome image: /nodejs-welcome:latest ports: - containerPort: 3000 --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: name: nodejs-welcome-service spec: selector: app: nodejs-welcome ports: - protocol: TCP port: 80 targetPort: 3000 type: ClusterIP EOF # 2.3 Create GitHub Actions workflow mkdir -p .github/workflows cat > .github/workflows/docker-build.yml <<'EOF' name: Build & Push Docker image on: push: branches: [ main ] jobs: build: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Checkout repository uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Set up Docker Buildx uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3 - name: Log in to Docker Hub uses: docker/login-action@v3 with: username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }} password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }} - name: Build and push image uses: docker/build-push-action@v5 with: context: . push: true tags: /nodejs-welcome:latest EOF # 3. Add all changed files git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml # 4. Commit & push git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow" git push origin main ``` Replace `` with your actual Docker Hub username before running the script. After the push, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically build and publish the Docker image. You can then deploy it to any Kubernetes cluster using `kubectl apply -f k8s/deployment.yaml`.
